task_description: Interview the user to clarify a new software project before producing an implementation plan or code.
initial_idea: Roamly: premium AI itinerary planner for shared leisure trips.

rounds.summary: Roamly supports destination discovery, AI itinerary generation, trip organization, saved places, budgets, collaboration, and memories. It specifies a polished mobile visual system and a broad screen inventory, but not target users, MVP boundaries, integrations, or success criteria.

V1 serves couples/groups planning short leisure trips. Its differentiated promise is realistic, high-vibe itineraries with intelligent pacing. The MVP centers on AI generation, drag-and-drop itinerary editing, and a daily route viewer; live booking/prices, social, concurrent editing, expenses, and memories are deferred. Native iOS/Android only; web sharing is read-only.

Creation begins with a structured form plus optional special requests. Partners can asynchronously vote, comment, and suggest places but the creator owns the itinerary. Realism depends on geographic clustering, travel time, pacing/buffers, hours, and reservation warnings.

Public secret links are view-only; feedback actions require a signed-in invitee. Apple, Google, and email magic-link auth are supported. Finalization locks new feedback, generates PDF/image and ICS assets, and enters active-trip mode. The owner can reopen; prior feedback persists or is archived when its stop is removed.

V1 is English-only across 20 tourist cities, supports six currency display preferences, uses offline trip briefs/static maps, and has affiliate-link tracking. The initially selected Google Places + Mapbox design conflicts with Google Places map-display and storage policies.

Mapbox-first, Supabase Auth, a $100–500 monthly ceiling, and partial-itinerary recovery are selected. Provider validation shows Mapbox POI storage and preview limits, Foursquare standard retention restrictions, and open-data gaps for live venue details; the product must now decide how strongly it promises opening hours/reservation data.

Venue facts are best effort with freshness labels and external verification links. Location is opt-in in active-trip mode with no background tracking. Public links are privacy-filtered. Account deletion hard-deletes personal/sole-owned data and transfers active collaborative trip ownership to the oldest active collaborator.

UI must use native tabs and NativeWind. Expo SDK 57's native tabs API imports from expo-router/unstable-native-tabs. NativeWind v4.2.7 has documented SDK 57 support; v5 remains release-candidate scope.

Standalone discovery is the first scope cut and nearby suggestions second; exports/offline briefs are protected. Success gates cover <=30s p90 generation, day pacing, 80% collaborative completion, and zero P0/P1 core-flow defects. Launch is an internal TestFlight/Play pilot for 100–250 users / 30–50 groups, then public listing.

codebase_context: Existing Expo 57 starter: Expo Router routes in src/app, single starter index screen; no project-specific behavior found.

pressure_pass.finding: Read-only access conflicts with partner actions that write votes, comments, and suggestions.

decision_boundaries.delegated: Select implementation details among declared stack choices, including backend/auth provider, database, AI model, analytics, monitoring, and Mapbox-first data integrations within budget. Use Expo Router native tabs and NativeWind.
decision_boundaries.requires_user: Any material cost, data-rights, or compliance issue.

open_blocker: Launch priority and testable success criteria
open_questions: whether the four-stop cap has a minimum
result: Interview complete; spec crystallized. No implementation plan or code has been produced.
